results.reason: The bank's 73% is not a self-rating figure at all (73% is the share with a favourable view of driving in a different YouGov survey). The direct poll asking 'How good a driver are you?' (YouGov Daily Question, UK adults) gives 22% 'probably above average' (48% average, 4% below, 22% don't drive, 4% don't know). Corrected to the real self-rating figure; population is UK adults, denominator is all people, which matches the question's wording.

results.newText: What % of people quit their New Year's resolution by the end of January?
results.reason: No published poll measures 'kept a resolution past February' exactly. The closest real stat from the same Forbes Health/OnePoll 2024 survey is that 43% quit by the end of January (23% quit within the first week; only 9% complete their resolutions). Reframed from kept-past-February to quit-by-end-of-January so the answer is the published figure.

results.newText: What % of Brits think they could qualify for the 2028 Olympics if they started training today?
results.reason: Searched for any poll on intending to run a marathon 'someday' — none exists; the only marathon stats are about people who have actually finished one (already covered by id 39). Reframed to the closest real overconfidence-in-sport poll: YouGov Aug 2024 found 27% of Britons said they would definitely/probably qualify for the LA 2028 Olympics in at least one of 25 sports if they started training today (n=2,070).

Searched 'survey percentage of people who can do a cartwheel' and variants. No survey or poll exists. The only numbers online are unsourced figures in social-media fitness videos, and they contradict each other (25%, 30% and 70% all claimed for the same feat), with commenters calling the numbers made up. Per the bar, REMOVE rather than keep an invented figure.

results.newText: What % of people say they like karaoke?
